text: I can feel their struggles, but they have the words in their head, but they just can't say it. Yeah. That's what makes me— Do you remember what that felt like? It felt like a ball stuck in your throat. Doesn't it get frustrating? Yeah, it does get frustrating after a while. Well, you're lucky because you got language, but there are kids at your age that still can't speak. Do I have autism still? Do you feel like you still have autism? Yeah, sometimes I do, but sometimes I don't. What do you mean? When do— I act a little crazy. Sometimes when I start to cry and feel sensitive, that's when I feel like I have autism. What about friendship? Yeah, that kind of feels like I have autism too. When I act cool around friends, that moment I don't seem to really have it. But do you sometimes feel like you don't have friends because you have autism? Yeah. You do? Yeah, sometimes I see people that don't like me sometimes because I have autism. Right. When you were little, you were really having a hard time connecting and making friends. They didn't understand who you were. Right? Yeah. What did they ask you to say? I asked you in the booty hall. Are you kidding me? You had boys that were sending you up to girls saying disgusting things. They make me go in the girls' bathroom. I did to make friends. Anytime you have someone that doesn't really understand you, they're not going to really know how to love you because they don't know who you are. I don't want you to feel sad about not having 25, 30 friends because you only really need one or two good friends, right? Yeah. Mom has Auntie Terry. I have Wonder. You have Wonder. You always look tall for me. Would Wonder ever put you in a bad position where you were either in harm's way or you did something inappropriate? He would never do that. No. That's a real friend. That is how you judge who is your friend, who has your back, who's looking out for you.
